data.source_title: Interprofessional communication supporting clinical handover in emergency departments: An observation study
data.source_setting: Two acute hospital emergency departments in Victoria, Australia
data.source_period: Published 2017; observation calendar dates not reported in abstract
data.source_n: 66 observed change-of-shift handovers; focus groups with 34 nurse participants
data.source_evidence_basis: Observations and focus groups; qualitative content and thematic analysis. Four structural components emerged: antecedents; behaviours and interactions; content; delegation of ongoing care. Infrequent/ad hoc interprofessional communication and discipline-specific content/processes emerged as risks; themes included standard processes, teamwork/interactions, and communication practices.
data.limitations: Qualitative findings from two Australian EDs and nurse focus groups; no frequency estimate or causal effect. Transfer to a US ED or any specific hospital requires local validation.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Optional synthetic variation can test whether a learner establishes handoff context, shares relevant content across roles, and clarifies ownership of ongoing tasks. This is a design inference, not a required universal handoff format.

provenance.acquisition_method: limited factual paraphrase of primary paper inspected by research agent
